newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rebound seen for HK's New World in fiscal 1996.
newsitem.headline: Rebound seen for HK's New World in fiscal 1996.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd is set to post a bounce-back in earnings for fiscal 1996, reaping profits from property development sales and exceptional items, analysts said on Monday.

The property investment and development company is due to release its 1995/96 (July-June) results on Thursday and analysts expect net profit of about HK$4.2 billion to HK$4.3 billion (US$538 million to US$551 million).
In fiscal 1995, New World reported a 20.6 percent drop in net profit to HK$3.41 billion. Interim net profit for fiscal 1996 was HK$1.70 billion compared to HK$1.61 billion the year before.

"I am expecting HK$4.2 billion net profit," said Nicholas Wong, property analyst at HSBC James Capel. "The year before they had a drop in property (revenues) because of a lack of property disposals. The development profit is back on track."

The main contributors to property sales are expected to be New World's Discovery Bay 4C development on Lantau island and two sites on Hong Kong island -- Blessings Gardens in Mid-levels and Li Chit Garden in Wan Chai.
"Basically, property development will account for about 32 percent of group pre-tax profit," said Carol Lai, research manager at SOCGEN-Crosby Securities.
Lai expected 22.3 percent growth in net earnings per share from HK$2.11 per share in 1994/95. Exceptionals would boost fiscal 1996 earnings, she said.
New World spun off its New World Infrastructure Ltd unit and Renaissance Hotel Group last year.
"There will be an exceptional of about HK$1.1 billion from the spin-off of New World Infrastructure and the hotel management (business) in the U.S.," said one analyst.
Lai said she expected the sale of Victoria Hotel in the Central district in fiscal 1996 to contribute HK$930 million in pre-tax profit.
Desmond Cheung, analyst at Vickers Ballas, said he was expecting net profit of HK$4.2 billion to HK$4.3 billion, with the major contributors being property sales, rental income and hotels.
"Rental income should grow mainly on the rental reversions from existing portfolios," he said.
Lai estimated HK$1.4 billion in net rental receipts, accounting for about 28 percent of New World's pre-tax profit.
"PRC (People's Republic of China) property sales will also be making a first-time contribution this year, although I think this is probably a wild card for the company," she said.
Lai said New World has pre-sold part of its infrastructure projects in China and could book HK$600 million in profits in fiscal 1996, although it may wait to book profits later.
Shares in New World Development hit an all-time high of HK$47.80 on Monday on expectations of strong earnings. The stock closed at HK$47.00, up HK$1.00.
Vickers Ballas said it had an "outperform" rating on the stock.
"The earnings quality is quite comparable to Sun Hung Kai Properties but it trades at a lower P/E (price/earnings ratio)," said Cheung.
He said while New World Development was trading at about 15 times prospective 1997 earnings, Sun Hung Kai Properties was trading at about 16 times.
Lai had a 12-month share price target of HK$55.
"I think after the results announcement there might be a consolidation in the share price. Over a 12-month outlook...you should not be looking at anything less than HK$55," she said.
